subject: 5 assumptions to verify before relying on a rental screen
preheader: a practical diligence checklist for the numbers behind the model.
headline: Five rental assumptions worth checking with property-specific evidence.
body: A preliminary result is only as useful as its inputs. Use this list to identify evidence that still needs to be collected before you rely on a rental model.

One: property tax. Review the local annual bill or a supported local effective rate, then investigate how the jurisdiction treats a sale, exemptions, and reassessment. TrueCap does not auto-fill a parcel-specific or post-sale tax amount.
Two: insurance. Replace any rough starting value with a current property-specific quote that reflects the intended occupancy, coverage, deductibles, and known hazards.

Three: rent. Separate advertised rent, a public benchmark, and reviewed comparable evidence. Account for concessions, condition, unit mix, utilities, and realistic downtime instead of treating a single listing as a lease outcome.

Four: management and leasing costs. Enter the actual fee structure you expect—including leasing, renewal, maintenance markup, and administrative charges where applicable—rather than assuming one percentage covers everything.

Five: DSCR that only meets the selected screening threshold at base-case rent. Lender definitions and minimums vary. Stress lower rent, then confirm the lender's written rent basis, DSCR calculation, leverage, reserves, and other program rules.

TrueCap exposes editable assumptions and shows how they affect modeled cash flow, cap rate, cash-on-cash return, and DSCR. It does not automatically verify these five items. Use the preliminary screen to organize diligence, then replace every material input with property-specific evidence.
signature_note: PS — keep your own reviewed source records alongside the model so each important assumption can be traced and updated.
